segments.text: Episode fourteen. Next stop... the Pillars of Creation.
These towers of gas and dust are the Pillars of Creation, inside the Eagle Nebula.
segments.headline: Inside the Eagle Nebula

segments.text: The tallest one is about four light-years long. Our whole solar system would be a tiny speck next to it.
They're about six and a half thousand light-years away.
Inside them, new stars are being born right now. Webb's infrared eyes can see through the dust to the young stars glowing inside.
segments.headline: Stars being born

segments.text: Hubble first photographed them in nineteen ninety-five, and it became one of the most famous space photos ever.
segments.headline: Famous since 1995

segments.text: Tomorrow, we meet a giant star that will one day explode. Next stop: Betelgeuse. Follow, so you don't miss episode fifteen.
